newsitem.title: UK: UK retail sales fall 0.3 pct in Sept.
newsitem.headline: UK retail sales fall 0.3 pct in Sept.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) released the following seasonally adjusted data on UK retail sales in September.
RETAIL SALES VOLUME SEPT AUG AUG(PREL)
Market forecasts had centred on a 0.1 percent fall in retail sales on the month and a year-on-year increase of 3.9 percent.
BY SECTOR (percentage gain, minus indicates fall)
The average weekly non-seasonally adjusted value of retail sales in September was 3.14 billion stg, 6.6 percent up on September 1995.
In value terms, retail sales rose 6.1 percent in the three months to end September on the same period a year earlier.
The ONS said the growth in retail sales for the three months to September versus the same period a year ago, at 3.4 percent, was the highest since December 1994.
The ONS said footwear sales, down 12.0 percent in value terms in September, exerted the major downward effect on the overall sales index.
The latest figures continued the upward trend in retail sales, the ONS said.
